subject.title: [Feature]: First-class org/team deployment — workspace scaffolding, RBAC, and deployment manifests

question: Which parts of first-class org/team deployment should OpenClaw core own now, and what security/config contract should define the first supported team or RBAC boundary?
rationale: The request would define new authorization, setup, and deployment guarantees across Gateway trust, sessions, tool policy, config, CLI, and docs; automation cannot safely choose that product/security boundary.

options.title: Decompose Under This Umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open and approve narrow sub-issues only after the threat model, config shape, precedence rules, and upgrade behavior are explicit.

options.title: Route Setup Outside Core
options.body: Keep core focused on missing auth/session/tool-policy APIs while scaffolding and manifests live in plugins, docs, or external deployment tooling.

options.title: Decline First-Class Team Mode
options.body: Document separate Gateways, trusted proxy, per-agent profiles, and sender policy as the supported pattern, then close this umbrella once maintainers make that decision.

recommendation.title: Decompose Under This Umbrella
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and approve narrow sub-issues only after the threat model, config shape, precedence rules, and upgrade behavior are explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the conversation capability foundation and Gateway trust-model documentation that frame this boundary.
